The Henon–Heiles describes a celestial system of ib example a star inside of a galaxy.

$$H(x,y,p_x,p_y)=\frac{(p_x^2+p_y^2)}{2m} + \frac{m\omega^2}{2}(x^2+y^2)+\alpha(x^2y-\frac{y^3}{3}).$$

---

We obtain the equations of motion by


::: {.columns}

::: {.column}
$$
\begin{align}
\dot{q_i} &=\frac{\partial H}{\partial p_i} \\
\dot{x} &=p_x/m \\
\dot{y} &=p_y/m

\end{align}
$$ 


:::

::: {.column}

$$
\begin{align}
\dot{p_i} &=-\frac{\partial H}{\partial q_i} \\
\dot{p_x} &= 
\end{align}$$

:::

:::

for canonical conjugate variables $(p_i,q_i)$ labeled by $i\in\mathbb{N}$. In our case simply $q_i\in\{x,y\}$ and $p_i\in\{p_x, p_y\}$

## Implementation

The resulting equation of motion in julia code:
```julia
function equations!(du, u, p, t)
    m, a, w = p
    x, y, px, py = u
    du[1] =  px
    du[2] =  py
    du[3] = -m*w^2*x - 2a*x*y
    du[4] = -m*w^2*y - a*(x^2 - y^2)
end
```
Here the potentials are defined:
```julia
potential(x, y; m=m, w=w, a=a) = m*w^2/2 *(x^2+y^2) + a*(x^2*y - y^3/3)

kinetic(px, py; m=m, w=w) = (px^2 + py^2)/(2*m)

hamiltonian(x, y, px, py; m=m, w=w, a=a) = kinetic(px, py, m=m, w=w) + potential(x,y, m=m, w=w, a=a)
```


And here the trajectory gets solved:
```julia
function solve_trajectory(u0; tspan=(0.0, 500.0), dt=0.1, p=param)
    prob = ODEProblem(equations!, u0, tspan, p)
    solve(prob, Vern9(), abstol=1e-10, reltol=1e-10, saveat=dt)
end
```
